assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy opened a new class of drugs for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with broad cardiometabolic benefit and very large clinical and societal impact. The discovery is clear, original and has visibly changed the field of metabolic medicine.
assessment.attribution: Holst characterized the proglucagon-derived GLP-1 peptides and their insulinotropic action, Mojsov identified and synthesized the active truncated GLP-1(7-36) form, and Drucker established GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology and its therapeutic translation. Knudsen's contribution is largely pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues, which I treat as less decisive for a discovery prize. Three-person configuration is plausible but credit among laboratories is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by multiple clinical programs and large outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between Mojsov, Habener-associated work (not on this list) and Holst is publicly contested.
Whether the committee would prefer to include the industrial development contribution of Knudsen is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, with clear change in oncology and cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain's early CD28-costimulated CARs, June's clinical translation of 4-1BB CAR-T in leukemia and Rosenberg's adoptive-cell-therapy and early CAR clinical work are each decisive for different parts of the story. Eshhar's foundational CAR concept is not among the credited names, which complicates a fully fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved products with multi-year follow-up and independent confirmation in several diseases; timely. Applications beyond hematologic cancers remain unproven.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR concept credit is not represented in the credited names.
Compound discovery: concept, costimulation and clinical translation may need different recognition.
Rosenberg's work is broader adoptive cell therapy, so its fit to the specific CAR discovery is partial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method to control defined cell types with light and has transformed causal neuroscience; the methodological impact is exceptional and widespread.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) was the decisive molecular step; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated its use in neurons and built the toolkit, and Miesenböck independently pioneered genetically targeted photoactivation. Six credited names exceed the three-person limit and force difficult choices; I favor molecular discovery plus the neuronal application.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and confirmed for over a decade; recognition is timely. Clinical translation is still early, which may weigh for or against.
uncertainties: Choice among six credited people is contestable; Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have strong claims.
Whether a methods/tool discovery fits the prize category as strongly as a disease mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling and a basic mechanism of proteostasis with implications for diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. Conceptually clean and original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori identified Ire1-mediated HAC1 splicing and the transcriptional program and gave the central pathway; the pair is a natural, compact configuration. Other contributors (such as Ron, Harding and Kaufman on PERK/ATF6 branches) are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over three decades and conserved in mammals; recognition is mature. Therapeutic translation is still limited.
uncertainties: Credit for mammalian branches of the response is not covered by the credited names.
Direct medical impact is less established than for therapeutic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR signaling defined the central controller of growth and nutrient response, with deep links to cancer, metabolism, aging and immunosuppression; very high impact and a clear discovery story.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and established it as a growth regulator; Schreiber's chemical biology on FKBP12-rapamycin helped identify the target in mammals. Sabatini's later mTORC1 nutrient-sensing work is important but I leave him out given the narrower and later contribution and his publicly known professional controversies, which I cannot fully verify. Other early contributors (Heitman, Movva, Sabatini, Brown) complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with extensive independent confirmation and clinical use of rapalogs; timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber and the mammalian target identification groups is not clean.
Facts regarding the controversy around one credited person are not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explained how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and interferon responses, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunotherapy and autoinflammation.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING as the adaptor. These are the two decisive contributions in my assessment, with Sun, Wu and Ishikawa as important contributors, possibly too many names for a prize.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation of the mechanism, but clinical translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) has not yet matured; recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is not yet demonstrated.
Credit for STING identification involved multiple groups, and the exact split is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition by imatinib proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy and transformed chronic myeloid leukemia into a manageable disease; a clear and lasting change in oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the discovery of the compound at Ciba-Geigy, Druker drove the clinical development and demonstration of efficacy, and Sawyers contributed to resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. The three-person configuration is plausible, though Sawyers' contribution is somewhat later and different in kind. Rowley and Witte/Baltimore's earlier BCR-ABL work is outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with more than two decades of survival data; recognition may be seen as long overdue and possibly partly addressed by earlier prizes in cancer genetics.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of the enabling genetics may overlap with this discovery.
Industrial credit (Lydon) in a discovery prize is a policy question for the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wnt signaling is a fundamental pathway in development, stem-cell renewal and cancer, discovered through the Int1/Wingless link between mouse mammary tumor virus and Drosophila segment polarity.
assessment.attribution: Nusse and Varmus discovered Int1 (Wnt1) and Nusse subsequently built the field on the signaling pathway; Varmus already shared a prize, which may weigh against his inclusion. Contributions by Wieschaus, Nüsslein-Volhard and Perrimon on wingless genetics are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed; therapeutic translation has so far been modest, but basic importance is clearly established.
uncertainties: Varmus has already been recognised, and the committee may prefer other configurations.
Roles of Drosophila geneticists in the pathway are not represented.
